title: Value categories (lvalues and rvalues)
recap: An expression has both a type and a value category. An lvalue identifies an object with identity; a typical rvalue is a temporary value such as a literal or arithmetic result.
A value parameter can be initialized from either kind of argument. Once inside the function, its name denotes a local object, so you can modify that object without modifying the caller.
objectives: Implement the stated behavior for multiple inputs.
Run the visible tests and explain one boundary case.
warnings: The function/type interface is fixed, but implementation syntax is your choice.
Do not remove the visible tests; the checker keeps an independent copy.
Respect the stated input domain and lifetime/range rules.
challenge: Implement nextTicket(current), returning the next integer ticket after current without changing the caller. Inputs are between -1000000 and 1000000. Practice incrementing the named local parameter, and compare calls using a named variable, a literal, and an expression. Each caller supplies a value; the parameter itself is a named lvalue inside the function.
hints: The return value is one greater than current.
The parameter is a modifiable local copy.
Do not introduce global or static ticket state.
